conceptCapsule.title: Kinematics in One Dimension: Calculus Formulation & Frame Transformations
conceptCapsule.summary: Motion is strictly relative to the chosen Frame of Reference. Distance ($s = \int |v| dt$) represents total trajectory path length ($s \ge 0$), whereas displacement ($\Delta x = \int v dt = x_f - x_i$) is a vector quantity ($|\Delta x| \le s$). For non-uniform acceleration, standard algebraic kinematic equations fail; one must integrate using $v = \frac{dx}{dt}$ and $a = \frac{dv}{dt} = v\frac{dv}{dx}$.
conceptCapsule.keyFormula: $$v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\text{Total Displacement}}{\text{Total Time}}, \quad \text{Average Speed} = \frac{\text{Total Distance}}{\text{Total Time}}, \quad a = v\frac{dv}{dx}$$
conceptCapsule.examTrap: When finding total distance from position functions $x(t)$, always locate the points where instantaneous velocity becomes zero ($v(t) = 0$) and sum up path segments between turning points. For motion under gravity passing a height $h$ at two different times $t_1$ and $t_2$, $h = \frac{1}{2}g t_1 t_2$ and initial velocity $u = \frac{1}{2}g(t_1 + t_2)$.

questions.statement: A particle moves along a circular path of radius $R$ from point $A$ to point $B$ subtending an angle of $120^\circ$ at the centre. The ratio of distance travelled to the magnitude of displacement is:
questions.solution:
1. Distance along circular arc: $$s = R \theta = R\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{2\pi R}{3}$$
2. Magnitude of displacement chord: $$|\Delta \vec{r}| = 2R \sin\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) = 2R \sin(60^\circ) = \sqrt{3}R$$
3. Ratio: $$\frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Displacement}} = \frac{2\pi R / 3}{\sqrt{3}R} = \frac{2\pi}{3\sqrt{3}}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A body starts moving from the origin along the $x$-axis according to $x(t) = 6t^2 - t^3$, where $x$ is in metres and $t$ is in seconds. The total distance travelled by the body before it momentarily comes to rest is:
questions.solution:
1. Velocity: $v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt} = 12t - 3t^2$
2. For momentary rest, $v(t) = 0 \implies 3t(4 - t) = 0 \implies t = 4\text{ s}$
3. Since $v(t) > 0$ for all $0 < t < 4\text{ s}$, motion is unidirectional.
4. Distance $= x(4) = 6(4)^2 - (4)^3 = 96 - 64 = 32\text{ m}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A person travelling along a straight road moves with speed $v_1$ for the first one-third of the total distance and with speed $v_2$ for the remaining two-thirds of the distance. The average speed of the person is:
questions.solution:
1. Let total distance be $s$.
2. Time taken: $t_1 = \frac{s/3}{v_1} = \frac{s}{3v_1}$, and $t_2 = \frac{2s/3}{v_2} = \frac{2s}{3v_2}$
3. Average speed: $$v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{s}{t_1 + t_2} = \frac{s}{\frac{s}{3}\left(\frac{1}{v_1} + \frac{2}{v_2}\right)} = \frac{3}{\frac{v_2 + 2v_1}{v_1 v_2}} = \frac{3v_1 v_2}{2v_1 + v_2}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A car travels along a straight line. For the first half of the total time of journey it moves with speed $40\text{ km/h}$ and for the second half time with speed $60\text{ km/h}$. The average speed of the car is:
questions.solution:
When time intervals are equal ($t_1 = t_2 = t_0$):
$$v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{s_1 + s_2}{2t_0} = \frac{v_1 t_0 + v_2 t_0}{2t_0} = \frac{v_1 + v_2}{2} = \frac{40 + 60}{2} = 50\text{ km/h}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: The position $x$ of a particle moving along a straight line varies with time $t$ as $x = \sqrt{a t^2 + 2b t + c}$. The acceleration of the particle is proportional to:
questions.solution:
1. $x^2 = a t^2 + 2b t + c$
2. Differentiating: $2x v = 2at + 2b \implies x v = at + b$
3. Differentiating again: $x a_{\text{acc}} + v^2 = a \implies x a_{\text{acc}} = a - v^2$
4. Substituting $v = \frac{at+b}{x}$: $$x a_{\text{acc}} = a - \left(\frac{at+b}{x}\right)^2 = \frac{a(at^2+2bt+c) - (at+b)^2}{x^2} = \frac{ac - b^2}{x^2}$$
5. $a_{\text{acc}} = \frac{ac - b^2}{x^3} \propto x^{-3}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Which of the following statements is ALWAYS TRUE for one-dimensional rectilinear motion?

options.text: Magnitude of displacement is equal to the total path length.
If speed is constant, acceleration must be zero.
If velocity is zero at an instant, acceleration must also be zero at that instant.
Average velocity is equal to the average of initial and final velocities.

questions.solution:
In purely 1D motion along a line, the particle cannot change direction without reducing its speed to zero. Thus, constant speed implies constant velocity vector ($v = \text{const}$), which strictly means acceleration $a = \frac{dv}{dt} = 0$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves along the $x$-axis such that its position is given by $x(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 2\text{ m}$. The total distance covered by the particle from $t = 0$ to $t = 5\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
1. Velocity: $v(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9 = 3(t - 1)(t - 3)$. Reversal occurs at $t = 1\text{ s}$ and $t = 3\text{ s}$.
2. Positions: $x(0) = 2\text{ m}$, $x(1) = 6\text{ m}$, $x(3) = 2\text{ m}$, $x(5) = 22\text{ m}$
3. Total Distance: $$s = |x(1) - x(0)| + |x(3) - x(1)| + |x(5) - x(3)| = |6 - 2| + |2 - 6| + |22 - 2| = 4 + 4 + 20 = 28\text{ m}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A passenger in a train moving at a constant velocity drops a coin. To the passenger, the trajectory of the coin appears as a vertical straight line. To an observer standing on the ground platform, the trajectory of the coin appears as a:
questions.solution:
In the ground observer's inertial frame of reference, the coin has initial horizontal velocity $u_x = v_{\text{train}}$ and vertical downward acceleration $g$. The parametric path is $x = v t$ and $y = \frac{1}{2}g t^2 \implies y = \frac{g}{2v^2}x^2$, which is a parabolic trajectory.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: The displacement $x$ of a particle moving in one dimension under the action of a constant force is related to time $t$ by $t = \sqrt{x} + 3$, where $x$ is in metres and $t$ is in seconds. The displacement of the particle when its velocity is zero is:
questions.solution:
1. $\sqrt{x} = t - 3 \implies x = (t - 3)^2$
2. Velocity $v = \frac{dx}{dt} = 2(t - 3)$
3. Setting $v = 0 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$
4. At $t = 3\text{ s}$, displacement is $x(3) = (3 - 3)^2 = 0\text{ m}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves in a straight line with constant deceleration. It covers $10\text{ m}$ in the $1\text{st}$ second and $6\text{ m}$ in the $2\text{nd}$ second. The particle comes to rest at time $t$ equal to:
questions.solution:
1. $s_n = u - \frac{a}{2}(2n - 1)$
2. $s_1 = u - 0.5a = 10$, and $s_2 = u - 1.5a = 6$
3. Subtracting gives $a = 4\text{ m/s}^2 \implies u = 12\text{ m/s}$
4. Time to stop: $t = \frac{u}{a} = \frac{12}{4} = 3.0\text{ s}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A ball is thrown vertically upwards from the ground with speed $u$. It passes a point at height $h$ at time $t_1$ on its way up and at time $t_2$ on its way down. The height $h$ is given by:
questions.solution:
1. Motion equation: $h = u t - \frac{1}{2}g t^2 \implies \frac{1}{2}g t^2 - u t + h = 0$
2. $t_1$ and $t_2$ are the roots of this quadratic equation in $t$.
3. Product of roots: $$t_1 t_2 = \frac{h}{\frac{1}{2}g} \implies h = \frac{1}{2} g t_1 t_2$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A point moves along a straight line such that its velocity is $v = v_0(1 - t/T)$ for $0 \le t \le T$. The total distance travelled by the particle in time $T$ is:
questions.solution:
Since $v(t) \ge 0$ over $0 \le t \le T$, distance equals displacement: $$s = \int_0^T v_0\left(1 - \frac{t}{T}\right)dt = v_0\left[t - \frac{t^2}{2T}\right]_0^T = v_0\left(T - \frac{T}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2}v_0 T$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: An elevator is accelerating upwards with an acceleration $a = 2\text{ m/s}^2$. A bolt falls from the ceiling of the elevator from a height of $2.4\text{ m}$ above the floor. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, the time taken by the bolt to reach the floor is:
questions.solution:
1. In elevator reference frame, effective downward acceleration is $g_{\text{eff}} = g + a = 10 + 2 = 12\text{ m/s}^2$
2. Using $h = \frac{1}{2} g_{\text{eff}} t^2 \implies 2.4 = \frac{1}{2}(12) t^2 = 6 t^2$
3. $t^2 = \frac{2.4}{6} = 0.4 \implies t = \sqrt{0.4}\text{ s} \approx 0.63\text{ s}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The acceleration $a$ of a particle moving along a straight line is given by $a = -k v^2$, where $k$ is a positive constant and $v$ is velocity. If initial velocity is $v_0$ at $t = 0$, the velocity at time $t$ is:
questions.solution:
1. $\frac{dv}{dt} = -k v^2 \implies -\frac{dv}{v^2} = k dt$
2. Integrating: $\left[\frac{1}{v}\right]_{v_0}^v = k t \implies \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{v_0} = k t$
3. $\frac{1}{v} = \frac{1 + k v_0 t}{v_0} \implies v = \frac{v_0}{1 + k v_0 t}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves along a straight line such that its velocity depends on displacement $s$ as $v = \alpha \sqrt{s}$, where $\alpha$ is a positive constant. The acceleration of the particle is:
questions.solution:
$$a = v \frac{dv}{ds} = (\alpha s^{1/2}) \frac{d}{ds}(\alpha s^{1/2}) = (\alpha s^{1/2})\left(\frac{1}{2}\alpha s^{-1/2}\right) = \frac{\alpha^2}{2}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A body dropped from a tower of height $H$ reaches the ground in $T$ seconds. The position of the body at time $t = T/3$ from the top of the tower is:
questions.solution:
1. Total height: $H = \frac{1}{2}g T^2$
2. Vertical distance fallen in $t = T/3$: $$y = \frac{1}{2}g\left(\frac{T}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{9}\left(\frac{1}{2}g T^2\right) = \frac{H}{9}\text{ below the top}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: For an object moving along a straight line, the ratio of magnitude of average velocity to average speed over any given time interval is:

options.text: Can be greater or less than $1$

questions.solution:
Because distance $\ge |\text{displacement}|$, we have: $$\text{Average Speed} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\Delta t} \ge \frac{|\text{Displacement}|}{\Delta t} = |\text{Average Velocity}| \implies \frac{|\text{Average Velocity}|}{\text{Average Speed}} \le 1$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A train of length $200\text{ m}$ travelling at $72\text{ km/h}$ overtakes another train of length $300\text{ m}$ travelling at $36\text{ km/h}$ in the same direction on parallel tracks. The time taken to completely cross is:
questions.solution:
1. Relative speed: $v_{\text{rel}} = 72 - 36 = 36\text{ km/h} = 36 \times \frac{5}{18} = 10\text{ m/s}$
2. Total distance to clear relative to each other: $L = 200 + 300 = 500\text{ m}$
3. Time: $t = \frac{L}{v_{\text{rel}}} = \frac{500}{10} = 50\text{ s}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The velocity-time relation of a body is $v = 3t^2 - 12t + 9\text{ m/s}$. The body changes its direction of motion at times:
questions.solution:
$v(t) = 3(t^2 - 4t + 3) = 3(t - 1)(t - 3)$. The velocity changes sign as it passes through zero at $t = 1\text{ s}$ and $t = 3\text{ s}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A bullet loses $\dfrac{1}{20}\text{th}$ of its velocity in passing through a wooden plank of thickness $d$. The minimum number of identical planks required to stop the bullet completely is:
questions.solution:
1. Velocity after 1 plank: $v_1 = u - \frac{u}{20} = \frac{19}{20}u$
2. Work-energy / kinematics: $\left(\frac{19}{20}u\right)^2 = u^2 - 2ad \implies 2ad = u^2\left(1 - \frac{361}{400}\right) = \frac{39}{400}u^2$
3. For $n$ planks to stop bullet ($v = 0$): $0 = u^2 - 2a(nd) \implies n(2ad) = u^2$
4. $n\left(\frac{39}{400}u^2\right) = u^2 \implies n = \frac{400}{39} \approx 10.25$
5. Therefore, a minimum of $11$ planks are required.
Therefore, Option A is correct.
